correctness.rationale: An independent exact computation identifies the frozen edge list with the two pentagonal rings of an icosahedron, enumerates faces by component unions, and performs top-down augmented integral unit elimination with a different pivot order. The stage-6 residual has six degree-3 and 26 degree-4 generators and no differential. Stage 5 has one generator in each of degrees 4 and 5 and thirty in degree 6, with a single coefficient -2 (the sign is basis-dependent). Unit elimination is integral: replace the pivot row basis vector by the normalized pivot column and clear its entry from the remaining columns. The chain identity splits off this two-term summand. Over F2, writing P for the stage-5 degree-5 boundary and Q for the stage-6 degree-4 boundary, the rank of the block map (P,i;0,Q) is 756; subtracting rank P=461 and rank Q=294 gives 1 on homology. Direct parity and span tests also validate the recorded 44-simplex cycle. Natural UCT applies with no H3 Tor term on either side, so the integral map is surjective with index-two kernel. The field H3 obstruction is below the pure dimension 5, which rules out shellability and Cohen–Macaulayness. No geometric collapse or wedge decomposition follows from the chain elimination.

value.rationale: The known torsion provides a reason to study these exact adjacent stages. The map answers whether the torsion class already has a lift from a torsion-free group at the preceding stage; stage-wise and rational data cannot answer this. The full integral calculation is also a reproducible nonshellable example on a natural graph.
